author: implementer
criterion: The target claims the nonce atomically with the effect; outcome recorded as a separate event. Lost acknowledgement gives UNKNOWN, resolved by receipt, never by retry; replay refused at the target on every boundary. Crash points tested are the named interruption points.

claim_patterns.same-transaction: Nonce INSERT, effect and receipt commit in one PostgreSQL transaction: no effect without its claim, no claim without its effect.
claim_patterns.claim-under-lock-then-create-only-effect: Nonce claimed under the target's exclusive lock before staging; the effect is create-only or identity-checked; a crash after the claim leaves the nonce spent and the target unchanged (fail-closed), never a second effect. Not a single atomic transaction.
claim_patterns.claim-then-governed-transaction: Nonce consumed and PREPARED logged before the host transaction applies effect and receipt atomically; a claim without preparation is UNKNOWN until reconciled; never re-executed.

notes: committed_ack_lost: redelivery after withdrawal returns the retained COMMITTED receipt.
spent_nonce_without_receipt: named point pack-bound-claimed-before-write; redelivery is UNKNOWN PACK_DELIVERY_RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED with no effect.

limits: effect-applied-connection-error-injected raises a synthetic psycopg.OperationalError after the real apply_on; it shows rollback and receipt classification of that error, not a severed or terminated transport.
Synthetic OperationalError after the real receiver transaction commits; not a killed transport.
Alert-store outage propagates an exception with no TARGET_UNKNOWN alert; the committed receipt remains authoritative.
Fresh receiver object and connections, not process restart; synthetic identities and no restricted-role claim.

boundaries.pattern: claim-and-spend-then-external-send (attempt record + budget unit + authority recheck in one transaction before the request)
boundaries.substrate: real PostgreSQL + synthetic receipt-v1 destination (no network)
limits: No atomic settlement with an external destination: the claim and spend commit before the request, and an unconfirmed send stays UNKNOWN until the destination's bound receipt resolves it.
Synthetic destination only; no real provider or network (governor 1e76307d).
Named interruption points only; no general crash-proof or distributed atomicity claim.
Filesystem crash simulation is an in-process non-recoverable exception at one named point, not an OS process kill; the PostgreSQL receiver has real process-kill evidence.
